meta.title: Operation of Hygrometer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To monitor and record relative humidity in the Pharmacognosy laboratory and crude drug storage areas to ensure optimal storage conditions and prevent moisture-induced degradation of crude drugs.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory, crude drug repository, herbarium rooms, and sample storage areas where humidity control is critical for drug stability.
procedure: Place the hygrometer at a representative location in the room — at bench level (1.0–1.5 m height), away from direct sunlight, air conditioning vents, or heat sources which give localised false readings.
For digital hygrometers: switch on and allow 10–15 minutes to stabilize before recording readings.
For analogue (hair or bimetallic) hygrometers: mount vertically and allow 30 minutes for equilibration after placement.
Read the relative humidity (RH%) from the display or dial.
Record the RH% and temperature readings in the environmental monitoring logbook at the required frequency: minimum twice daily (morning and afternoon) for GMP-grade storage areas.
Also read and record the ambient temperature simultaneously — RH and temperature data are interdependent.
If RH exceeds the acceptable range (typically 40–65% RH for general crude drug storage), take corrective action: activate dehumidifier, improve ventilation, or relocate moisture-sensitive samples.
If the hygrometer displays an alarm or out-of-range symbol, investigate the cause and take corrective action before the next reading.
Calibrate the hygrometer at specified intervals using a salt calibration kit or by comparison against a reference calibrated instrument.
Record calibration dates and results in the instrument calibration log.
Replace batteries when indicated; for analogue instruments, have the instrument serviced annually.
precautions: Do not expose the hygrometer to direct liquid water or condensation — sensor damage is irreversible.
Do not place near heat sources, windows, or HVAC outlets — these give localised false readings unrepresentative of the room.
Allow adequate equilibration time before recording — insufficient equilibration gives inaccurate baseline readings.
Calibrate at least once every 6 months or per institutional policy — hygrometer sensors drift over time.
For critical storage areas (stability chambers, reference standard storage), install continuous data-logging hygrometers and set alarms.
Document all out-of-specification readings and the corrective actions taken.
